rows.Origin:
Bred by Tim Hermann Kordes (Germany, 2001).
Introduced in South Africa by Ludwig's Roses in 2015 as 'Pink Ayoba'.
Introduced in Australia by Treloar Roses in 2021 as 'Pink Ayoba'.
rows.Bloom: Deep pink. None / no fragrance. 17 to 19 petals. Average diameter 2.25". Medium, semi-double to double, flat bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season. Pointed, ovoid buds.
rows.Habit:
Bushy, upright. Semi-glossy, medium green, leathery foliage. 5 leaflets.

Height: up to 2' (up to 60cm). Width: up to 20" (up to 50cm).
rows.Patents:
United States - Patent No: PP 24,604 on 8 Jul 2014 VIEW USPTO PATENT
Application No: 13/507,533 on 6 Jul 2012
The new variety of rose plant of the present invention originated from a controlled crossing in a breeding program of two distinct parents during the summer of 2001. The crossing was between an ‘un-named seedling’, the seed parent, and another ‘un-named seedling’, the pollen parent, from the same inventor.
